clue.text: Maybe there's still life in what they do

definitions.text: Maybe there's still life in what they do

parts.words: Maybe there's still life in what they do
parts.note: reads like praise for old folk who remain lively, but a still life is a painting of fruit, flowers and the like, so it is the work of painters

explanation.surface: A cheery remark that some people are still full of vigour in their activities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still life' looks like 'still alive'; it is the genre of painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters and other creators produce still lifes, so a still life may be in their work.

clue.text: A large majority? Not quite

parts.note: L is the clothing abbreviation for large
most is the greater part, a majority

explanation.surface: A question about a big majority, answered that it falls short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' looks like a comment on the question; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly but not entirely is the meaning of this adverb.

clue.text: Find a match here? This can flame up quickly

definitions.meaning: a dating app where people look for a romantic partner
dry kindling material used to start fires

explanation.surface: Talk of searching for a match to start a quick fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry kindling catches fire fast; the dating app of the same name pairs up couples.

clue.text: One now weak, having given out on behalf of church

parts.note: money given out is spent
for means on behalf of
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone now frail after giving everything for the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or thing that has lost its power or influence is described by this phrase.

clue.text: Rush of crowd needs some calmness urgently

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A crowd pushing forward needs some calming down at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft had 'needs' in the definition; it is a link word, since a surge is a rush of crowd, not of crowd needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden forward movement of a mass of people is a sweeping rush.

clue.text: Circus artiste's value is tumbling

parts.note: reads as a falling price, but it says that a certain circus performer is valued for doing somersaults and rolls

explanation.surface: The worth of a circus performer is collapsing, like a share price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tumbling' looks like a falling value or an anagram signal; it is the performer's skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus artiste whose skill is tumbling is a gymnastic performer of flips and balances.

clue.text: Ordering heralds back to military town

indicators.note: ordering things puts them in a new arrangement
back says the little word to is read from right to left

explanation.surface: Instructions to heralds to return to a garrison town.
explanation.walkthrough: ALDERSH comes from 'Ordering' heralds; 'back' turns to into OT. Aldershot is a Hampshire town, home of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: This Hampshire town is famous as the home of the British Army.

clue.text: Space for one's elbow?

parts.note: from the phrase elbow ..., sufficient space to move freely

explanation.definitionFit: Space in general is a synonym, and elbow plus this word is a phrase for freedom to move.

clue.text: Glad beer is brewed by the Danube

definitions.note: a place situated on the river; the clue names it by location

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Cheerful news that ale is made beside a great river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serbian capital stands where the Sava meets the Danube.

clue.text: Film or plays, right?

parts.note: a child who toys with something plays with it
a Tory is right-wing, a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A question whether one means the cinema or the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is only a link; Tory is the everyday name for a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1995 Pixar animation was the first computer-animated feature film.

clue.text: Chap's first to enter minister's home

parts.note: a chap is a man, so chap's gives the possessive with its S

indicators.note: first says to take only the opening letter of the word enter

explanation.surface: A man is the first to go into the clergyman's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is only a link joining the pick to the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish Presbyterian minister's house is traditionally called by this name.

clue.text: Drama one never sees performed

parts.note: a play that is performed but never seen, because it is heard over the airwaves

explanation.surface: A play so obscure that nobody ever gets to watch it on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A play broadcast on the wireless is performed for listeners, so nobody sees it.

clue.text: Wee darling?

parts.note: a little loved one; read as a phrase it is wee inside sweet and heart, a lover

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' is hidden inside 'sWEEtheart', and the whole word means darling, so the clue points both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A darling is a beloved person, a term of endearment for a lover.

clue.text: Like some wine? It's no end crude!

indicators.note: no end says the final letter of the word for crude is dropped

parts.note: a brute is a crude, coarse person

explanation.surface: An exclamation that some wine is very rough indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' looks like 'endlessly' as intensifier; it cuts the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Very dry champagne and sparkling wine is labelled with this French term.

clue.text: Not feeling well, with no more anagrams to do?

definitions.meaning: slightly unwell or in a bad mood

definitions.text: with no more anagrams to do?
definitions.meaning: anagram indicators often say sort, so having used them all one has run short of sorts

explanation.surface: A crossword solver feeling poorly after finishing all the anagrams.
explanation.definitionFit: Being off-colour or grumpy is an idiom; sorts are mixes, so none left is the jokey sense.

clue.text: Turn one's back on the roast second time round?

definitions.meaning: to snub or ignore someone deliberately
a joint of roast meat served chilled the next day

explanation.surface: Someone shunning the Sunday roast when it reappears as leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub is an idiom about coldness; leftover roast lamb is a literal chilled joint.

clue.text: Letters on keyboard can be low

definitions.meaning: keys are pushed down when typing

explanation.surface: Typed characters may appear in a muted, downbeat mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Keys pushed down when typing are one sense; feeling glum or downcast is the other.

clue.text: New coins, one's obsession

parts.note: euros are European coins
one is I, and the apostrophe-s gives S

explanation.surface: Someone fixated on the latest money.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosis is a mental disorder that can involve compulsive fixation or anxiety.

clue.text: Hymn is horrible — cancel it

indicators.note: something horrible is a mess, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A churchgoer complaining about a bad hymn and wanting it dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A song or chant with a biblical text, used in church services, is a religious song.

clue.text: Given this freedom, name optician at random

indicators.note: letters placed at random are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Liberation will come if you pick some eye specialist by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given this' is a link that makes the definition read on.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberation from bondage, as of slaves, is a synonym for being set free.

clue.text: Specimen, small, more than enough

parts.note: S is the clothing abbreviation for small
ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: A list of contradictory descriptions of a test sample.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a small portion taken as an example for testing.

clue.text: Film director, finally failing, took place in the ranks

indicators.note: finally failing says the director's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Federico Fellini was the Italian director of La Dolce Vita

explanation.surface: A movie director whose final work flopped joined the army.
explanation.definitionFit: To form up in line in military drill is the phrasal verb meaning take one's place.

clue.text: Routine hard for girl

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine one is stuck in
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A dull schedule is tough on a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, as of the biblical heroine, is a stock crossword example.

clue.text: Settle area, wild land

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: An instruction to colonise a region of untamed country.
explanation.definitionFit: Property in the form of land and buildings is called by this term.

clue.text: Tree that's between poplar and chestnut

indicators.note: says to keep only the letters where the two tree names meet, setting aside the joining word in the middle

parts.note: the run from the end of the first tree to the start of the second spans the little joining word

explanation.surface: A tree described as somewhere between two others in a wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' looks like a place in the wood; it takes the end of 'poplar' joined to the start of 'chestnut', skipping 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciduous conifer that sheds its needles in winter is this tree.

clue.text: Feature of river no end odd

indicators.note: no end says the last letter of the word for odd is removed

parts.note: weird means odd, strange

explanation.surface: A river with endlessly strange characteristics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end odd' looks like 'very odd'; 'no end' cuts the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A low dam across a river to control its flow is a common river feature.

clue.text: Win gold: I follow

definitions.note: a noun; the clue lets the person speak, saying they come after another

parts.note: a win is a success
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone vowing to imitate a champion who takes first place.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the person themselves speaking: one who comes after.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir who comes after another in office could say of themselves that they come next.

clue.text: Drive back to dance round piano

indicators.note: round says the dance word goes around the piano letter

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: An instruction to return and dance about a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: To repulse an attacker is to force them to retreat.

clue.text: Second vegetable, like a tomato, taken on fork

parts.note: a pea is a green vegetable
a ripe tomato is red

explanation.surface: A dinner-table scene of vegetables being eaten off a fork.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiked or pierced on a prong, as food is when eaten with a fork.

clue.text: Banshee terrified failing man

definitions.note: a person whose career is over

indicators.note: something terrified is shaken up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A wailing spirit frightens a man who is weakening.
explanation.definitionFit: A faded figure no longer successful is a washed-up person.
